overall: As of 09:39 ET (6:39 AM PT), Los Angeles is sitting in a marine layer with the current temp at 62.6°F and a running max of only 64.9°F, achieved at 00:52 ET — very early in the day. The low ceiling (305m), elevated dewpoint (59°F, only ~3.6°F below air temp), and slightly negative velocity over the last 30 minutes (-0.6°F/hr) confirm suppressed overnight marine influence. The day is well behind typical warming pace for early July, but the bulk of the diurnal heating window remains ahead with the NWP-modeled peak not expected until 15–16h ET (noon–1 PM PT).
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models are in reasonable agreement but show a meaningful spread: GFS (73.0°F) and HRRR (73.3°F) run notably warmer than ECMWF (70.6°F) and NBM (68.8°F), with the official NWS text calling 70°F. The Intraday model is likely being pulled artificially low by the current marine-layer-suppressed observations and should be discounted in favor of the META model, which strongly favors 72–73°F at 57.8% on even buckets and implies 71–72°F for the active odd-bucket market.
max_temp_prediction: The marine layer is expected to erode through late morning PT, allowing temperatures to climb into the low-to-mid 70s by early afternoon — consistent with the GFS/HRRR guidance and the META model's strong lean toward 72–73°F. For the active odd-bucket market, the 71–72°F bucket carries the highest probability at 41.9%, and the overall evidence (model consensus, META signal, NWS narrative) supports a best estimate near 71.5°F, with moderate-to-high confidence given Tier 1 ensemble signals and a manageable timing spread of 1.1h.
